blocks.text: קְרוֹבוֹת לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: Page number 50 is printed in both outer corners. It is not part of the text.

blocks.text: תַּאֲלַת זוּ כְּחָפֵץ לְהַתְעִיל. שׁוּעַ עֲרוֹךְ לִמְּדָם לְהוֹעִיל. רוֹן הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם הַמּוֹעִיל. קְרוֹא בְּגָרוֹן מוֹקֵשׁ לְהַגְעִיל׃ צִדְקָם לְהַקְפּוֹת בְּנִיב שַׁוְעָה. פָּעֳלָם בְּקֶרֶב שָׁנִים לְשַׁמְּעָה. עֵת רָצוֹן וְיוֹם יְשׁוּעָה. סְבִיכַת קֶרֶן וּבְרִית שְׁבוּעָה׃ נוֹבְבִים בְּגִישַׁת חוֹתָמוֹת תִּשְׁעָה. מִסְפַּר שָׁתוֹת וְחוֹתָמֵיהֶן תִּשְׁעָה. לְמִנְיַן פִּלּוּל שֵׁמוֹת תִּשְׁעָה. כְּחִנְּנָה עֲקָרָה יָלְדָה שִׁבְעָה׃ יַאֲמִירוּ עֹז מַלְכִיּוֹת עֶשֶׂר. טְבוּעוֹת לְשֵׁם בֻּחַן בְּעֶשֶׂר. חֹק זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְקוֹלוֹת עֶשֶׂר. זֵכֶר מְבָרֵךְ גְּבִיר
uncertainties: לִמְּדָם: I can't clearly read the vowel under the lamed. It could be hiriq or sheva. The dagesh and sheva in the mem are also unclear, and the word might read לְמֹדָם.
הַרְרֵי: the vowels under the hey and the first resh are unclear. It might read הֲרֲרֵי.
לְהַקְפּוֹת: there seems to be a dagesh in the pe. That is unexpected and should be checked.
לְשַׁמְּעָה: the vowel under the shin and the dagesh/sheva in the mem are unclear.
כְּחִנְּנָה: the letters I read are כחננה, with two nuns. The hiriq under the het and the dagesh/sheva in the first nun are uncertain. It is not כחנה.
עֹז: the holam dot over the ayin is faint.
מַלְכִיּוֹת: the vowel under the kaf could be hiriq or qubuts.
בֻּחַן: the vowel under the bet is unclear. It could be qubuts (בֻּחַן), sheva or segol.
Every period on this page is printed as a small diamond. I have written it as an ordinary period.
This is a printed alternative reading (כ״א) for the word just before it, גְּבִיר. It appears in small type inside the line.

blocks.text: בְּעֶשֶׂר׃ וְיִפֶן בְּאָהוּב אֲתוּי נַהֲרַיִם. הֶעָקוּד בְּהַר מוֹר אֲחוֹרַיִם. דִּשְׁנוֹ יֵרֶא לָחֹן שִׁירַיִם. גָּשִׁים עָדָיו בֹּקֶר וְצָהֳרָיִם׃ בְּזֶה פֶּרֶק חִנֵּן עֲתִירָה. בְּעַד אֲסוּרָה עַד הֻתָּרָה.
uncertainties: וְיִפֶן: the segol under the pe is faint.
לָחֹן: the holam dot on the het is uncertain.
עֲתִירָה: the vowel under the tav is faint.
הֻתָּרָה: the qamats under the tav could also be read as sheva.
This siglum is printed in the middle of the line, before the closing couplet.

blocks.text: אֶנְקַת אָסִיר אָז כְּהֻכְתָּרָה. אֵלַי לְהֵעָתֵר כְּמוֹ נֶעְתָּרָה׃
uncertainties: כְּהֻכְתָּרָה and נֶעְתָּרָה: next to the qamats under the tav there is a small vertical stroke that may be a meteg (כְּהֻכְתָּֽרָה, נֶעְתָּֽרָה). I have left it out of the text. Please verify.

blocks.text: מֶלֶךְ בְּדִין עֲלוֹת בִּתְרוּעָה. גֵּיא עִם דָּרֶיהָ לְרוֹעֲעָה.
uncertainties: גֵּיא and עִם: the vowels under the gimel and the ayin are faint.
This siglum is printed in the middle of the line, before בַּשּׁוֹפָר.

This is a conditional alternative for Shabbat, printed in small type. It replaces בַּשּׁוֹפָר. The first small word looks like מַח, but it is probably an abbreviation or a misreading. It might be a cue such as בשבת: or ביום שבת. Please verify against the scan. שַׁבָּת may be unpointed in the print.
The sof pasuq colon is printed directly after אֲפַתֶּנּוּ, before the variant in parentheses. That placement is odd, but I have kept it as printed.
This is a printed alternative reading (כ״א) for אֲפַתֶּנּוּ.

blocks.text: וּבְבֶרֶךְ כְּרִיעָה. בְּטַלְלֵי תְּחִי בְּגַנּוֹ אֶתְרוֹעֲעָה׃
uncertainties: אֶתְרוֹעֲעָה: there is a mark below the resh/vav area that may be a meteg (אֶתְרֽוֹעֲעָה). I have left it out of the text. Please verify.
בְּטַלְלֵי: the vowel under the first lamed is faint. It could be sheva or patah.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer of the New Year
uncertainties: Page number 50 is printed in both outer corners.

blocks.text: When He wished to heal the folly of His people, He taught them to arrange prayer so that it should be of help, the valued prayer of the primaeval mountains, to call aloud in order to scare the accuser. He taught them to affirm their righteousness with an outburst of entreaty, to recall at a time of favour and on the day of salvation their toil over the years, the ram caught in the thicket, the covenant and the oath. They recite the prayer with nine benedictions, nine is the number of blessings and their endings, according to the names of God in that prayer which the childless one (Hannah) uttered, who later gave birth to seven children. They revere in ten verses the acknowledgment of divine rule, they are based on him who was ten times tested (Abraham), the measure of remembrance and of Shofar tones is ten in memory of him who with ten blessings made his son master. May He gaze upon the beloved son of him who was brought out of Mesopotamia, who was bound hand and foot on Mount Moriah, let Him behold his ashes so as to be gracious to his descendants, who approach Him morning and noon. On this day he (Isaac) fervently entreated on behalf of his childless wife, until she too was remembered. As the sighs of the childless one were answered then, so let my prayer too be heard as hers was heard.

The King rises in judgment with the loud blast to shake the earth with its inhabitants, but with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him, and with bent knee in the dew of revival will I sound in His garden the shattering tone.
uncertainties: Over "the Shofar" in line 2 there are stray marks above the letters, like a macron or dots. They look like print or scan artifacts and are not diacritics. I have ignored them.
The words "(the memory of the Shofar)" translate the Hebrew Shabbat alternative and are printed in the running English text.

notes: I read both full pages and all eight enlarged bands. Where bands overlap, the shared lines were checked against the full page and transcribed only once.

s128 has no rule, so I read the whole page. It contains two piyyut units. The first, תַּאֲלַת, is a reverse-alphabet acrostic (תשר״ק), as the heading ע״ס תשר״ק says. Its letters run ת ש ר ק / צ פ ע ס / נ מ ל כ / י ט ח ז / ו ה ד ג / ב א, and it ends with a closing couplet (אֶנְקַת … נֶעְתָּרָה) marked ק׳. The second unit is the מֶלֶךְ stanza.
In this print the speaker siglum ק׳ (congregation) appears four times: at the start of תאלת, before אֶנְקַת, at the start of מלך, and before בַּשּׁוֹפָר.

There are three printed conditional alternatives: (כ״א גְּבִירוֹ) for גְּבִיר, (כ״א אֲרַצֶּנּוּ) for אֲפַתֶּנּוּ, and a Shabbat alternative (… בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר) for בַּשּׁוֹפָר. I could not read the opening cue word of the Shabbat alternative with confidence (it looks like מַח).
I saw no Biblical cantillation on s128. Apart from the possible metegs flagged above, the pointing is ordinary nikkud.

Proposed corrections, not applied to the text: (1) The colon after אֲפַתֶּנּוּ comes before the parenthesized alternative. That may be a typesetting oddity; it could be meant to follow it. (2) If the dagesh in לְהַקְפּוֹת is real, it may be a typo.

The English translation leaves out no stanzas. It covers both units, and the Shabbat alternative is given in parentheses. The Hebrew linkage cues תאלת and מלך are recorded separately from the English prayer text.
